# Power and precision: single-model rates and the hint effect

*Generated by `analysis/power_hint.R`. Do not edit by hand.*

All results are for 3 samples per prompt, intra-scenario correlation 0.3 and 4,000
simulations per cell. Intervals and tests use scenario-level means, so the scenario is
the unit (t interval and paired t-test, two-sided, 5%).

## 1. Precision of one model's detection or false-alarm rate

Half-width is the average distance from the estimate to either end of the 95% interval.
Coverage is how often the interval contains the true rate (target 95%).

## 2. Hint effect: power of the planned design (15 scenarios)

The hint effect is detection at the direct level minus detection at the neutral level.
The two hint levels of one model are assumed to correlate 0.7 across scenarios, and part
of the scenario-to-scenario variation in the hint effect is shared by all models.

| Detection when cued | True hint effect | Power, one model | Power, pooled over 4 models |
|---|---|---|---|
| 70% | 10 points | 17% | 39% |
| 70% | 20 points | 45% | 91% |
| 70% | 30 points | 78% | 100% |
| 70% | 40 points | 96% | 100% |
| 90% | 10 points | 22% | 60% |
| 90% | 20 points | 61% | 98% |
| 90% | 30 points | 89% | 100% |
| 90% | 40 points | 98% | 100% |
